objectives: Quantify cross-lingual reasoning capability when integrating English SEC filings with multilingual news evidence.
Isolate performance degradation between single-document factual retrieval and multi-document analytical reasoning.
Measure evidence grounding quality under multilingual noise using ROUGE-1 against expert references.
Analyze sensitivity of model accuracy to linguistic heterogeneity and document fusion complexity.
research_gap: Financial QA benchmarks predominantly evaluate monolingual retrieval or reasoning, ignoring multilingual evidence fusion.
Existing evaluations conflate language understanding with reasoning, lacking controlled separation of factual retrieval versus analytical synthesis.
No benchmark systematically measures robustness of evidence grounding when supporting documents span heterogeneous languages and sources.
problem_statement: It is unclear how reliably language models can align, integrate, and reason over semantically related financial evidence distributed across multiple languages and documents.
There is no standardized evaluation protocol to quantify reasoning degradation induced by cross-lingual evidence aggregation.
The absence of controlled difficulty stratification limits interpretability of model reasoning failures.

research_questions.text: How does cross-lingual evidence integration affect answer accuracy compared to monolingual financial QA baselines?
What performance gap emerges between factual retrieval (PolyFiQA-Easy) and analytical multi-document reasoning (PolyFiQA-Expert)?
How sensitive is ROUGE-1 performance to linguistic diversity in the supporting document set?
To what extent do generated answers preserve explicit evidence grounding under multilingual context expansion?

hypotheses.text: ROUGE-1 scores decrease significantly when multilingual evidence is introduced compared to monolingual-only inputs.
Performance degradation is larger for PolyFiQA-Expert than for PolyFiQA-Easy due to multi-hop reasoning demands.
Linguistic heterogeneity increases hallucination and reduces lexical alignment with expert references.
Models exhibit weaker evidence grounding when required to reconcile conflicting or redundant multilingual sources.

expected_contributions.text: A controlled evaluation framework isolating multilingual fusion, reasoning depth, and grounding reliability in financial QA.
Quantitative characterization of reasoning degradation across language diversity and task difficulty.
Error taxonomy linking failure modes to linguistic alignment, document fusion, and reasoning complexity.
Reproducible protocol for evaluating cross-lingual reasoning beyond surface retrieval accuracy.
